one_month_reasoning: No earnings fall in the window: Q3 FY27 results are due in early December, and Dreamforce and Investor Day (mid-September) are already past. Four things do fall inside it. (1) The final settlement of the $25B ASR in October: about 34M more shares, which is known and mechanical. (2) The Contentful ($1.5B) and Fin/Intercom ($3.6B) closes, which the 10-Q expects in Q3 FY27 and which are already in guidance. (3) Peer software earnings in late October (ServiceNow, Microsoft), which have moved CRM on seat-compression headlines this year. (4) The FOMC. None of these supports a directional call. The stock has already fallen about 14% from its $268 intraday high on Sep 3 and bounced off $225 on 9/29, so neither momentum nor reversal is strong enough to lean on. I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred on about $231.8 with 12.5% monthly sigma, a little under the 47%/3.5 rule because realized vol was inflated by the H1 2026 crash. This is unchanged from round 1, and the supervisor's reconciled view agrees.

fair_value.method: A 50/50 blend of two methods. P/E: 14x a Sep-2027 NTM core EPS of about $17.3 (1/3 FY28 $16.1 + 2/3 FY29 $17.85 on about 785M post-ASR shares) = $242. SBC-burdened FCF yield: NTM FCF about $17.1B less SBC about $4.8B (9% of revenue) = $12.3B, over 787M shares, at a 6.5% yield = $240. The skeptic adjustments are an un-rerated 14x multiple, SBC treated as a real cost, and a slightly below-supervisor FY28 net income growth.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM core non-GAAP EPS at Sep-2027 of about $17.3 (1/3 FY28 $16.1 + 2/3 FY29 $17.85) x 14x

inputs_detail.value: $16.67-$16.71 on 838M diluted shares, including $2.98/sh of H1 strategic-investment gains

inputs_detail.derivation: ($16.69 - $2.98) x 838M. The Q2 interest expense of $473M is a full quarter of the March-2026 notes, so interest is already in the run-rate.

inputs_detail.value: about 787M at settlement; about 785M FY28 average
inputs_detail.derivation: The 10-Q says the ASR delivered 103M shares at $198.34, about 80% of the expected total. At the roughly $182 expected average, $25B buys about 137M shares, so about 34M more arrive in October; 821M (Q2 diluted) - 34M = 787M. Open-market buybacks roughly offset SBC dilution in FY28 while $5.1B of cash goes to Contentful and Fin.

Core net income +10% to about $12.65B: revenue about +9-10% (7-8% organic plus Contentful and Fin), a small margin gain, and forgone interest income on $5.1B of deal cash. Divided by 785M shares. This is a little below the supervisor's $16.3 because I shade organic growth, and it is in line with the consensus of about $16.0.
Net income +9% plus about 1.5% net buyback shrink, for about +10.9%. The ASR benefit is not counted twice: only ongoing buybacks enter FY29.

The stock trades at about 14.4x FY28 consensus today; BofA cited 14x forward in May, and the June trough was about 10x. Organic growth is only 7-8%, leverage is up (Moody's A2), and the seat-compression question is unresolved, so I assume no rerating. I stay at 14x rather than the supervisor's 14.5x; that difference is about $9/share.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF at Sep-2027 of about $17.1B minus SBC of about $4.8B = $12.3B owner FCF; 787M shares; 6.5% required yield

inputs_detail.derivation: FY28 is about $16.2B (FY27 $15B +8%, after about $1.9B/yr of interest) and FY29 about $17.5B (+8%). NTM = 1/3 FY28 + 2/3 FY29.

The FY27 margin bridge puts SBC at 9.0% of revenue ($4.96/sh). Applied to NTM revenue of about $53B. The 10-Q shows $2.9B of FY28 expense from existing grants alone, before new grants, so 9% is a fair run-rate.
Post-settlement count, as in the P/E method.

About $39B of debt ($25B of March-2026 notes plus a $6.0B 2026 term loan, per the 10-Q debt table) and about $28B net debt before the $5.1B of deal cash. Moody's cut the rating to A2 (stable) because of the debt-funded buyback, and the terminal value is contested by AI seat compression. The supervisor uses 6.4%; the difference is small.

bear.story: The second-half organic reacceleration fails. Organic growth slips to about 6%, CIO spend-cut surveys (KeyBanc, Bernstein) show up in cRPO in the December or February print, Agentforce ARR growth reads as repackaging (its definition was widened in Q2), and the engineering leadership handover slows AIforce delivery. The multiple compresses to about 10x a FY29 core EPS of about $15.5, near the June 2026 trough ($146-178) and BofA's $160 target.

base.story: Organic growth holds at 7-9%, Contentful and Fin add about 1.5pts of inorganic growth in FY28, margins hold at about 34-35%, and the post-ASR share count of about 787M lifts NTM core EPS to about $17.3. The multiple stays at about 14x.

bull.story: Strong NNAOV (the best in four years) turns into visible organic reacceleration to 10%+, Agentforce plus Data 360 ARR scales, and seat-compression fears fade. The market rerates to about 18-19x NTM EPS of about $17.5.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $160 (about 9.3x NTM core EPS of $17.3 and about 10x FY28 core EPS, near the June 2026 trough and BofA's target), the market would be pricing actual seat-base decline or a failed H2 organic reacceleration: cRPO well below the ~14% guide, or an FY28 guide under ~8%. That is the AI seat-compression bear case showing up in the numbers rather than just in the multiple. At that level the $25B ASR (average about $182) would also be well underwater on about $39B of debt, which would limit further debt-funded buybacks.

Q4 FY27 earnings and initial FY28 guidance. Informatica (closed Nov 2025) anniversaries during Q4, so organic growth becomes visible in headline growth, partly masked by Contentful and Fin in FY28

key_uncertainties: Whether organic growth (about 7-8% implied by the Q3 guide) actually reaccelerates in H2 FY27 as management promised
Whether seat compression from AI agents shows up in renewals: CIO surveys (KeyBanc) point to net spend cuts, while management's self-reported seat growth and record-low attrition are unquantified
Quality of the Agentforce ARR metric, whose definition was widened in Q2 FY27 to include Slackbot and Headless 360
Execution risk from the President/Chief Engineering and Customer Success Officer stepping down (effective 2026-08-06), with a successor who joined in June now owning Agentforce/AIforce delivery
Balance-sheet leverage after the $25B debt-funded ASR plus a $6B term loan (Moody's A2), plus $5.1B of cash going to Contentful and Fin
Size of the data-breach class action. The 10-Q says no security incident has so far had a material financial impact, which caps how much weight I put on it
reasoning: Round 2, skeptic lane. The supervisor's fact checks changed three inputs. (1) Shares: the 10-Q confirms 103M ASR shares delivered at $198.34, about 80% of the total, so about 34M more arrive in October and the post-settlement count is about 787M, not 800M. (2) NTM EPS: my round-1 FY29 of +9% left out ongoing net buybacks and any margin gain. Rebuilt from FY27 core net income of about $11.5B ($13.7 core EPS ex the $2.98 of gains x 838M), I get FY28 of $16.1 and FY29 of $17.85, so NTM is about $17.3 (the supervisor has $17.5; I shade organic growth slightly). (3) Catalyst timing: Informatica anniversaries in Q4 FY27, not Q1 FY28, and Contentful and Fin then add inorganic growth in FY28, so my 'tailwind removed' catalyst was mis-timed. I also add the engineering-leadership departure (8-K 2026-08-05), which I missed and which fits my lane: an orderly succession, but more execution risk during the reacceleration test. On sources: I verified the Moody's downgrade to A2 (stable outlook, March 2026) through a ratings-news listing rather than only the Simply Wall St recap, so I corrected my round-1 wording that paired A2 with a negative outlook. I could not find S&P's negative-outlook action in a primary source; it rests on a press recap, so it does not move a number. The 10-Q adds a $6.0B 2026 term loan on top of the $25B of notes and says no security incident has had a material financial impact to date, which tempers the breach-litigation risk. Revalued: P/E 14x $17.3 = $242; SBC-burdened FCF yield ($17.1B - $4.8B)/787M at 6.5% = $240; blended fair value about $241, up from $236. I disagree with the supervisor on the multiple (14x, not 14.5x) and keep my 6.5% yield: with organic growth at 7-8%, higher leverage and the seat debate unresolved until the December print, I do not assume a rerating. Scenarios: bear $155 / base $245 / bull $325 at 25/50/25, for a mean of about $243. The ladder is a lognormal with median about $236 and sigma about 0.39, with a slightly fatter left tail for leverage and the binary seat-compression outcome and a slightly trimmed right tail. The 1-month ladder is unchanged. Research this round was limited to one 10-Q fetch and four web searches/fetches; the Moody's summary page and cbonds returned stale or 403 content.
